 Online shopping is becoming increasingly expensive.
 The average value of each product sold on e-commerce platforms has increased continuously over the past three quarters, while the low-priced product segment has shrunk and products priced over 1 million VND are increasingly dominant.
 ZNews • 28/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The value of goods traded on e-commerce platforms in Vietnam is trending upwards.
 According to data from the data aggregation and mining platform Metric, in the third quarter of 2026, total sales across the four e-commerce platforms Shopee, TikTok Shop, Lazada, and Tiki reached VND 150,380 billion , a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, the volume of products sold reached nearly 1.09 billion, only a 10% increase.
 Calculations based on these two indicators show that the average value of each product sold on e-commerce platforms in the third quarter reached approximately 138,100 VND, an increase of nearly 32% compared to the same period in 2025.
 Notably, this is not an isolated development in the third quarter, but rather a trend that has been emerging for over a year now.
 Average product value increased for three consecutive quarters.
 According to Metric data, in the first quarter of this year, total sales across the four e-commerce platforms reached VND 148,580 billion with approximately 1.14 billion products sold. The average value per product was approximately VND 130,500.
 In the second quarter, market sales decreased by nearly 4% to VND 143,010 billion , while consumption volume fell to approximately 1.05 billion products. The average value per product increased to approximately VND 136,400, nearly 5% higher than in the first quarter.

 This trend continued into the third quarter, with the average value reaching approximately 138,100 VND, an increase of over 1% compared to the second quarter.
 Thus, after three quarters, the average value of each product sold on e-commerce platforms has increased by nearly 6%, equivalent to approximately 7,600 VND per product.
 Overall, in the first nine months of the year, total sales across the four platforms reached nearly 442 trillion VND , an increase of over 44% compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, the volume of products sold reached nearly 3.28 billion, an increase of 12%.
 The large discrepancy between sales growth rate and output indicates that the scale of transactions expanded not only due to the number of products sold, but also due to an increase in the average value of goods.
 You may also like The market for low-priced items is shrinking, while the price of products over 1 million VND is increasing sharply.
 The trend of increasing product value is also clearly reflected in the changes in sales structure by price segment.
 According to Metric, in the third quarter, products priced above 1 million VND contributed 19% of total sales across the four e-commerce platforms, an increase of 4.5 percentage points compared to the same period last year. This segment also recorded the largest increase in sales share among the price groups surveyed.
 Conversely, the product group priced under 100,000 VND saw its sales share decrease from 24.4% to 19.3%.
 Similarly, the 100,000-200,000 VND price segment also decreased from 25.7% to 22.9%.
 Thus, the two product groups priced under 200,000 VND only contributed a total of 42.2% of e-commerce sales in the third quarter, a sharp decrease compared to 50.1% in the same period last year. 
 Cheap products on e-commerce platforms are gradually losing their market share. Photo: Metric. 
 Conversely, the product group priced at 200,000 VND or more increased its sales share from 49.9% to approximately 57.8%.
 Not only the segment above 1 million VND, but also the mid-range and near-premium price groups have seen an increase in market share.
 Specifically, the 200,000-350,000 VND price segment increased from 16% to 17.2%; the 350,000-500,000 VND price group increased from 8.9% to 9.3%.
 Meanwhile, the sales share of products priced between 500,000 and 750,000 VND increased from 6.6% to 7.7%, while the group priced between 750,000 and 1 million VND increased from 3.9% to 4.6%.
 Data shows that consumer patterns on e-commerce platforms are clearly shifting towards higher-value products, while the sales contribution of low-priced goods is gradually shrinking.
 From an industry perspective, the upward trend in transaction value is also reflected in the difference between sales growth rate and production volume.
 You may also like For example, in the third quarter, the Fashion Accessories group recorded sales of over 34% year-on-year, but consumption volume decreased by nearly 8%.
 Similarly, stationery sales increased by over 53% despite a nearly 7% decrease in volume. The pet care group also saw a more than 38% increase in sales while product volume decreased by nearly 7%.
 In the major product categories, Beauty continued to lead the market with sales of nearly VND 24.379 billion , an increase of nearly 41% compared to the same period last year. This was followed by Home & Living with over VND 20.041 billion , an increase of over 48%, and Women's Fashion with nearly VND 17.465 billion , an increase of nearly 48%.
 In particular, the Department Store - Food sector recorded a sales increase of over 80%, reaching approximately 11,456 billion VND , while production volume increased by nearly 50%.
 This development shows that the Vietnamese e-commerce market is entering a growth phase that is not only based on expanding the number of products sold, but also linked to an increase in the value of goods traded.
